subject: Audit intake: scope clarification, pen-test fallback and order-form updates

Subject: Initial audit questions and pen-test window

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helix is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before procurement moves this forward we need to close a couple of compliance items tied to our enterprise onboarding: SOC 2 evidence access, preferred pen-test timing, and how audit requests are scoped.

Attached is a short questionnaire with our typical asks (Helix_Audit_Questions.pdf). High level:
- We need to confirm what evidence can be provided vs. what requires a scoped inspection.
- Pen-test: do you allow customer-directed penetration tests? If so, what staging options and windows do you offer?
- For SOC 2: can you provide a recent report and a summary of the control ownership areas?

Can we schedule a 30-min call this week with your security and legal folks to align? Sarah (procurement) is cc'd.

Thanks,
John

John — quick summary from Security so the call is productive. See attached short SOC 2 bundle (SOC2-summary.pdf) that covers:
- Type II period and control ownership map (what Redwood controls vs. customer responsibilities).
- Typical artifacts we can share on request (logs, configuration snapshots, test evidence) with redaction for customer data.

Pen-test options:
- Customer-directed tests: allowed only against an agreed staging environment or ephemeral tenant; production is not permitted.
- Staging access: we provide a read-only staging snapshot and a limited-hours interactive window under supervision for the duration of the test.
- Scheduling: standard windows are weekdays 9am-5pm PT; for high-risk checks we require 48-hour notice and a scoped testplan.

Evidence cadence recommendation (what we propose adding to the Order Form / Security Exhibit):
- SOC 2 Type II report: provided post-signing (redacted) with an SLA for delivery (30 days).
- Artifact requests: 2 business days turnaround for standard artifacts; 7 business days for deeper sampling/forensic logs.
- Inspection requests: limited to 1 inspection per 12-month period unless escalated under an exception clause.

I realize Helix may ask for different timing — happy to discuss and adjust. Attaching the SOC summary and examples of the artifacts list.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)

John / team — legal perspective and proposed MSA redline approach (high level):

Proposed principles to add to the Security Exhibit / Order Form appendix:
- Scope-limited inspections: Customer inspections must be limited to pre-defined artifacts and sampled data sets; no direct or persistent access to production systems or customer data.
- Notice and plan: Customer must provide a written scope and test plan 72 hours before any interactive activity; Redwood reserves the right to deny or limit activities that risk production stability.
- Frequency cap: Limit to one inspection per rolling 12-month period; additional inspections require a justified exception and senior security approval.
- Pen-test fallback: If the customer requires an external pentest, it must be conducted on a staging or ephemeral tenant and follow an agreed statement of work; Redwood will provide a list of approved testing providers if requested.
- Confidentiality & reporting: All findings to be shared via secure channel; Redwood will provide remediation timelines for critical findings and will not disclose internal remediation details beyond impact summaries.

Suggested contract language snippet (for redlines):
"Customer may request inspection of Supplier's controls as set forth in the Security Exhibit. Such inspection shall be limited to the artifacts and sample sets expressly listed in the Exhibit and shall not include live production access. Supplier shall reasonably accommodate inspections subject to (i) prior written notice and a mutually agreed scope; (ii) Supplier's right to prohibit or limit activities that would materially risk production stability; and (iii) a frequency cap of one (1) inspection per twelve (12) months absent written exception."

I'll produce a marked-up version of the MSA and a tracked Order Form appendix (proposed_orderform_redlines.docx) by EOD so procurement can review. If Helix needs different frequency or access, let's surface that on the call and we'll note it as a commercial exception.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference

John / Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Laura and Karthik's input we've got an approach that should meet Helix's requirements without exposing production or operational risk. Summary / next steps:

1) Karthik will upload the redlined MSA + Order Form appendix (proposed_orderform_redlines.docx) to this thread — please review and flag any commercial exceptions by EOD Monday 10/18.
2) Laura will share the SOC2 bundle (attached) and the artifact list; standard SLA: 2 business days for routine artifacts, 7 for deeper logs.
3) Pen-test: Helix can run a customer-directed test only against a scoped staging tenant; we'll need a 72-hour scope and 48-hour operational notice depending on the tests listed.
4) If Helix requests a higher inspection frequency or production-adjacent access, we will treat that as an exception and route to commercial for approval.

Proposed meeting: Thu 10/14 at 11:00 AM PT — invite sent separately. If that time doesn't work, Anna on procurement suggested Fri 10/15 morning.

I'll also create the DocuSign envelope and HubSpot deal task once the redlines are agreed. Links will be posted here.

Thanks — look forward to getting Helix onboarded.
